title: company-wide-policies-and-processes-2027-06-15
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended as the single reference for employees and managers to ensure consistent, auditable, and compliant behaviors across teams.

Scope

Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and vendors with access to Redwood systems, facilities, or financial processes. Exceptions must be approved by the policy owner team and recorded in the related_pages section.

Roles and Ownership

- Policy owner: People Ops (primary contact: Aisha Patel)
- Access approvals: Team manager + Security (for elevated access)
- Procurement approvals: Finance + Hiring manager (per table below)
- Change management owner: Eng Platform (operational playbooks)
- Data steward: Product/Applied ML teams for model/data-specific assets

1) Access and Permissions

Objective: Grant the minimum privileges necessary (principle of least privilege), ensure timely revocation, and maintain an auditable trail for access changes.

Process:
1. Request: All access requests must be submitted via the Access Request form (Confluence link / internal Jira project ACC-REQ). Include justification, duration, and owner.
2. Approval: Manager approves routine access. Elevated privileges (admin, service account creation, production database) require Security review and documented justification.
3. Provisioning: IT or on-call SRE executes provisioning through IaC or identity provider (Okta) automations. Manual changes must be logged.
4. Review: Quarterly access reviews by owner_team and team managers; immediate revocation on offboarding.

Access approval matrix:
| Resource Type | Approver(s) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Internal tools (confluence, jira) | Manager | Self-service where available |
| Production clusters / Databases | Manager + Security | MFA + scoped role required |
| Service accounts & API keys | Security + Eng Platform | Keys must be bound to rotation schedule |
| Customer data access | Manager + Data Steward + Security | Additional NDA/MFA requirements |

Temporary access: Maximum 30 days unless explicitly extended. Extensions must be documented and re-approved.

2) Change Management

Objective: Ensure safe, auditable changes to systems that affect availability, security, or data integrity.

Change types:
- Standard (pre-approved, routine)
- Minor (non-customer impacting, low risk)
- Major (customer-impacting, high risk)

Change workflow (numbered):
1. Create change request ticket in CHG (change management board) with rollback plan and test plan.
2. Impact assessment and risk rating by owner.
3. Approvals: Minor changes require team lead + risk owner; Major changes require Eng Platform + SRE + Product sign-off and a scheduled maintenance window.
4. Communication: Notify affected customers/internal stakeholders 72 hours before Major changes, 24 hours for Minor.
5. Implementation: Follow runbook and canary rollout policies where applicable.
6. Post-change review: Document outcomes within 48 hours; link to incident tracker if issues occurred.

Emergency changes: Documented in emergency CHG ticket within 24 hours, with automated rollback where possible.

SLOs and thresholds for change windows:
- Maximum change window for Major releases: 4 hours planned maintenance (exceptions escalated)
- Deployment success target: 99.9% of canary instances pass health checks before broader rollout

3) Data Management

Principles:
- Data classification: public / internal / restricted / confidential.
- Minimize PII exposure and follow retention schedules.
- Use approved storage classes and encryption at rest and in transit.

Key procedures:
- Data inventory: Each team maintains a data asset register in the Data Inventory doc.
- Retention & deletion: Follow the retention schedule table below; deletion must be auditable.
- Access controls: Restricted datasets require RBAC and documented purpose for access.
- Backups: Nightly backups for production databases; monthly restore tests.

Retention schedule (examples):
| Data type | Retention | Owner |
|---|---:|---|
| Logging (non-sensitive) | 90 days | Eng SRE |
| Audit logs | 3 years | Security |
| Customer PII | Retain only as needed per contract | Product/Data Steward |
| Model checkpoints (non-sensitive) | 180 days | Applied ML |

Encryption & key management:
- Use company KMS for all secrets and keys. HSM-backed keys for production crypto where required.
- Rotate encryption keys annually or on compromise.

Data breach response:
1. Triage (Security) 
2. Containment and evidence collection
3. Customer notification per contractual obligations (consult Legal)
4. Post-incident review and remediation plan

4) Procurement and Expenses

Objective: Centralize vendor spend controls, ensure approvals, and support timely reimbursement.

Procurement workflow:
1. Request: Submit Purchase Request (PR) via procurement portal with business justification, estimated cost, and vendor details.
2. Approval thresholds:
   - < $1,000: Manager approval
   - $1,000 - $25,000: Manager + Finance
   - > $25,000: Manager + Finance + VP approval + Legal review (contract required)
3. Purchase order issuance and tracking by Finance.
4. Receipt and acceptance: Team confirms delivery and quality.
5. Invoice processing: Finance matches invoices to PO and releases payment net-30 unless otherwise negotiated.

Expenses & reimbursements:
- Use company card where available. Submit expense forms within 30 days with receipts.
- Per diem and travel limits in travel section.
- Non-compliant expenses will be returned for correction.

5) Vendor Management

Vendor classification:
- Strategic (long-term, critical)
- Operational (regular suppliers)
- One-off (ad-hoc purchases)

Onboarding checklist for vendors:
1. Vendor intake form completed (procurement portal).
2. Security review for vendors with access to systems or data; require SOC 2 or equivalent for Strategic vendors.
3. Legal contract with clear SLAs, termination clauses, and data handling requirements.
4. Finance set up for payments and tax forms.
5. Assign vendor owner and review cadence.

Vendor review cadence:
- Strategic: Quarterly business review and annual security/contract re-evaluation
- Operational: Semi-annual review
- One-off: Ad-hoc review as needed

Offboarding: Revoke access, collect company assets, and confirm final invoices and data deletion per contract.

6) Travel Policies

Booking & approvals:
- All travel must be booked through the approved travel portal or travel manager (unless explicitly approved).
- Domestic travel: Manager approval required.
- International travel: Manager + People Ops approval; ensure passport/visa plans are documented.

Spending limits & per diems:
- Economy class for flights under 6 hours; premium economy with manager approval.
- Hotel maximum: $250/night standard rate for major metro hubs (higher with approval).
- Meals: per diem $75/day domestic, $100/day international unless receipts submitted for actuals.

Safety & compliance:
- Employees traveling on company business are covered by the company travel insurance; register travel plans with People Ops.
- For high-risk locations, additional approvals and security briefings are required.

Expense submission:
- Submit travel expenses within 10 business days of return with itemized receipts.

7) Internal Templates and Form Library

This section centralizes canonical templates to ensure consistency across teams. Templates are stored under Confluence > policies-and-process > templates. Key templates:
- Access Request Form (template)
- Procurement Request (PR) template
- Vendor Security Assessment checklist
- Change Request / Runbook template
- Data Retention & Deletion Request form
- Travel Authorization and Expense form

Template governance:
- Templates are owned by People Ops and respective owner teams (Security for security-related forms, Finance for procurement).
- Updates to templates require review by at least two reviewers and are versioned in the template page.

Audit, Compliance & Review Cadence

- Annual policy review owned by People Ops with representatives from Security, Finance, Legal, and Eng.
- Quarterly spot audits for access reviews, procurement POs, and vendor security evidence.
- Maintain an audit log of policy changes and approvals; archived versions retained for 3 years.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q: Who do I ask for a temporary access extension?
A: Request via Access Request form and include duration; manager + Security will approve.

Q: What counts as a Major change?
A: Any change that can impact customer experience, data integrity, or security controls. If unsure, submit a CHG ticket and flag for Major review.
